result.question: Research the current (as of September 2026) landscape and ecosystem of the "pi" agent family by Mario Zechner (badlogic) — the pi coding agent / pi-mono monorepo (https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono, npm @mariozechner/pi and related packages) — as a candidate primary coding-agent platform, plus its interactive "Pi Agent UI" surface for agentic work. Deliverables: (1) a map of the pi family as it exists today — the coding agent CLI/TUI, the agent UI (web or desktop), pi-ai SDK/library, proxy/pods/other packages, release cadence, maintenance health, docs quality; (2) a survey of the open-source community ecosystem around pi — extensions, plugins, themes, MCP integrations, third-party tools, notable forks, community hubs (Discord/discussions), and which community assets are worth adopting; (3) a hard-requirements gap analysis against these MUST-HAVEs: (a) hooks comparable to Claude Code covering ALL FOUR: pre-tool-call permission gating, post-edit format/lint/test triggers, session lifecycle events (start/stop/compaction), and outward notifications/observability — pi's "extensions" mechanism may be the answer, verify what it can actually intercept today; (b) proper context management including automatic context compaction when nearing the window limit; (c) session management (persist, list, resume/continue sessions); (4) cross-platform viability on BOTH macOS and native Windows (win32, not just WSL) for the CLI and the UI; (5) provider support: OpenAI via Codex subscription (openai-codex provider), LOCAL models (ollama / llama.cpp / LM Studio / vLLM), and general multi-provider switching ergonomics (Anthropic, Google, etc.), including auth paths. Compare briefly against Claude Code where a gap exists. End with concrete recommendations: what to adopt now, which community extensions/tools to leverage, what gaps need custom extension work, and any dealbreakers. Prioritize primary sources: the pi-mono repo (README, docs/, CHANGELOG, extension API source), Mario Zechner's blog/mastodon posts, npm, and real community artifacts over secondhand blog coverage.
result.summary: Pi is a viable primary coding-agent candidate as of 2026-09-01, but the research question's premises are stale: the project moved on 2026-05-07 from badlogic/pi-mono to earendil-works/pi and from npm @mariozechner/* (deprecated) to @earendil-works/*, where it is very actively maintained (~100k stars, latest publish 2026-08-28, push on the research date). The three MUST-HAVE capability areas verify well: automatic context compaction is built-in and default-on (reactive + proactive, extension-customizable), session management is first-class (JSONL tree files with continue/resume/fork/branch navigation), and provider support covers OpenAI Codex subscription login, Anthropic/Copilot subscriptions, 30+ API-key providers, first-class llama.cpp, and ollama/LM Studio/vLLM via OpenAI-compatible custom providers. Hooks are the qualified area: pi deliberately ships no core permission system ("No permission popups" philosophy), but the extensions mechanism verifiably intercepts tool_call with blocking semantics (a first-party permission-gate example ships), supports custom compaction and MCP integration — while post-edit triggers and outward-notification hooks were not explicitly verified and need direct confirmation against docs/extensions.md. Cross-platform is confirmed for the CLI on macOS and native win32 (dedicated windows.md, Git Bash dependency for the bash tool); the "Pi Agent UI" surface is only a lagging component library (pi-web-ui, last published 2026-05-27), not a verified standalone app. Recommendation: adopt via @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent, budget custom extension work for the full four-hook parity with Claude Code, and treat the UI surface and community-extension inventory as open diligence items.

findings.claim: STALE PREMISE (foundational): the pi project migrated on 2026-05-07 from Mario Zechner's badlogic/pi-mono to the Earendil Works org (earendil-works/pi, canonical long-term home), and all npm packages re-scoped from @mariozechner/* (now deprecated, frozen at 0.73.1 with pointer messages) to @earendil-works/*. Every map, health check, and adoption decision must target the new repo and scope; old GitHub URLs still redirect but the old npm scope is genuinely frozen since May 2026.
findings.evidence: GitHub API resolves badlogic/pi-mono to full_name "earendil-works/pi"; pi.dev announcement: "Pi has moved to its new long-term home under the Earendil Works organization"; all 270+ @mariozechner versions carry "deprecated: please use @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent instead going forward"; Zechner's own post: "The GitHub repository moves from badlogic/pi-mono to earendil-works/pi." A refuted claim (0-3) that the new name is @earendil/pi confirms the exact scope is @earendil-works, not @earendil.

findings.claim: FAMILY MAP: the monorepo's primary published packages are @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent (interactive CLI, bin "pi"), pi-agent-core (agent runtime, tool calling, state), pi-ai (unified multi-provider LLM SDK), pi-tui (terminal UI with differential rendering), pi-telemetry, and pi-web-ui (reusable web chat components). Slack/chat automation was split to a separate repo, earendil-works/pi-chat. Caveat for the "Pi Agent UI" ask: pi-web-ui is a component LIBRARY, not a standalone agent-UI app, and it lags the family (0.75.3, last published 2026-05-27, vs 0.84.4 on 2026-08-28 for the core four).

findings.claim: HOOKS MUST-HAVE (the qualified area): pi deliberately has NO built-in permission system — launched in "full YOLO mode" (Nov 2025) and the current philosophy section still says "No permission popups. Run in a container, or build your own confirmation flow with extensions." The extensions mechanism (TypeScript modules, landed ~2026-01-05 via PR #454) is the answer and verifiably covers pre-tool-call gating: docs/extensions.md specifies tool_call "(can block)" with return contract { block: true, reason?, terminate? } and fail-safe blocking on handler error, and a first-party permission-gate.ts example ships. Custom tools, custom compaction/summarization, MCP server integration, and event handlers are all documented "What's possible" items. NOT explicitly verified in surviving claims: post-edit format/lint/test triggers, full session lifecycle events (only session_before_compact is evidenced), and outward notification/observability hooks — these need direct confirmation and likely some custom extension work for Claude Code parity.
findings.vote: 3-0 on the verified parts (merged: #9, #20, plus #15); coverage of all four hook types is NOT fully established
findings.evidence: README line: "No permission popups. Run in a container, or build your own confirmation flow with extensions"; extensions doc: "tool_call (can block)", "Return values from tool_call control blocking via { block: true, ... }", "tool_call errors block the tool (fail-safe)"; launch post: "pi runs in full YOLO mode... without permission checks or safety rails." Compaction customization hook session_before_compact confirmed in docs/compaction.md. Gating is real interception, but opt-in extension loading — nothing is gated by default.

findings.claim: CONTEXT-MANAGEMENT MUST-HAVE: SATISFIED. Automatic compaction is built in and enabled by default, triggering reactively on context overflow (recovers and retries mid-run) AND proactively when approaching the window limit (contextTokens > contextWindow − reserveTokens, default reserve 16384), with manual /compact (including custom instructions) and extension-customizable behavior via session_before_compact (can cancel or supply a custom summary).
findings.evidence: README: "Automatic: Enabled by default. Triggers on context overflow (recovers and retries) or when approaching the limit (proactive)." Verifier's adversarial issue sweep found only provider-specific edge bugs (Ollama error-string matching #2626 closed, mid-tool-loop check #2871 closed, reasoning-model input-cap overshoot #3765) — mechanism existence and default-on status uncontested.

findings.claim: SESSION-MANAGEMENT MUST-HAVE: SATISFIED. Sessions auto-save as JSONL tree files (id/parentId entries) under ~/.pi/agent/sessions/ organized by working directory, with pi -c (continue most recent), pi -r and /resume (browse/select/delete), /fork and --fork <path|id>, /clone, --session, --no-session, HTML export, and in-place branch navigation via /tree — capability confirmed both in docs and in the locally installed pi 0.80.9 binary's help output.
findings.evidence: README: "Sessions auto-save to ~/.pi/agent/sessions/ organized by working directory" and "Sessions are stored as JSONL files with a tree structure... enabling in-place branching without creating new files"; only counter-evidence ever found was #320 (--resume wrong dir), closed with a one-line fix in Dec 2025.

findings.claim: PROVIDER MUST-HAVE: SATISFIED, including the openai-codex path. Subscription logins: Anthropic Claude Pro/Max, OpenAI ChatGPT Plus/Pro (Codex), GitHub Copilot. ~30-31 API-key providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure, Gemini, Vertex, Bedrock, DeepSeek, Mistral, Groq, Cerebras, xAI, OpenRouter, Fireworks, Together, ...). Local models: llama.cpp router is FIRST-CLASS (/login llama.cpp, /llama model management, docs/llama-cpp.md); ollama/LM Studio/vLLM are NOT named built-ins but work via ~/.pi/agent/models.json custom providers speaking a supported API (OpenAI/Anthropic/Google) — docs/providers.md gives an explicit Ollama example (localhost:11434/v1, api openai-completions) with Ollama/vLLM compat flags. pi-ai adds cross-provider context handoffs, a designed-in feature for mid-session model switching. Official local-LLM provider extensions are a live community request (issue #4155); a third-party pi-ollama-provider exists.
sources: packages/ai/README.md ("Any OpenAI-compatible API: Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio, etc."; OpenAI Codex OAuth provider)
findings.evidence: README verbatim: "Subscriptions: Anthropic Claude Pro/Max, OpenAI ChatGPT Plus/Pro (Codex), GitHub Copilot"; "Pi also supports the llama.cpp router server. Configure it with /login llama.cpp"; "Add providers via ~/.pi/agent/models.json if they speak a supported API (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google)." The Nov-2025 post lacked the Codex path; the current pi-ai README has since added "OpenAI Codex (ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription, requires OAuth)" — the gap closed upstream.

findings.claim: MCP STANCE: no MCP in core, by explicit design (context-cost rationale: MCP tool descriptions burn "7-9% of your context window... before you even start working"; Nov 2025: "pi does not and will not support MCP"). The stance holds as of Sept 2026 for core, but the extension path is deliberately open: the README's extensions "What's possible" list includes "MCP server integration", and badlogic himself opened issue #563 (2026-01-08) proposing an MCP extension example. Read as: no ambient MCP tax, MCP available opt-in via extension when needed.
findings.evidence: Post gives concrete numbers (Playwright MCP 21 tools/13.7k tokens; Chrome DevTools MCP 26 tools/18k tokens) and the CLI-tools-with-READMEs alternative; the 2026 repo README contains no core MCP support and no shipped MCP extension example among 80+ examples — extension-path-open, not ecosystem-wide ban.

findings.claim: CROSS-PLATFORM MUST-HAVE (CLI): macOS and native win32 both supported. Author's stated support: "Runs on Windows, Linux, and macOS (or anything with a Node.js runtime and a terminal)"; the repo ships dedicated docs/windows.md documenting NATIVE win32 operation (Git Bash discovery at C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe, optional built-in PowerShell tool via pwsh.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive, Windows-style shellPath config) — WSL appears only as a PATH fallback, not the mechanism. Node >=20.6.0 (old line), no npm "os" restriction; Windows-specific keybinding notes in README; a live user report (#2839) confirms native win32 (not WSL) operation in Windows Terminal in 2026. Practical caveats: the bash tool needs a bash.exe (Git for Windows suffices), one minor open win32 paste bug (#2839), and the newer releases appear to raise the Node floor (legacy-node20 dist-tag exists). UI-surface Windows viability is NOT established (no verified standalone UI app at all).
sources: npm registry @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent 0.73.1 manifest (engines, no os field)
findings.evidence: windows.md is a real native-operation doc, not a "use WSL" punt — verifier explicitly tested that adversarial angle and it failed. Zero hits for "experimental"/"unsupported" regarding Windows in the README.

findings.claim: COMMUNITY ECOSYSTEM SUBSTRATE: pi has a first-party packaging/distribution mechanism ("pi packages") bundling exactly four resource types — extensions, skills, prompt templates, and themes — shareable via npm or git (npm:@foo/bar@1.0.0, git:github.com/user/repo@v1, plus local paths), with gallery preview metadata; this plus the official Discord is the substrate for the extension ecosystem. Security note: packages run with full system access. Concrete community artifacts surfaced only incidentally in verification (s1lver091/pi-agent-config, a third-party pi-ollama-provider, issue #4155 requesting official local-LLM provider extensions); no verified inventory of mature adoptable community packages exists in the surviving claims.
findings.vote: 3-0 on the substrate (#6); ecosystem inventory itself unverified
findings.evidence: packages.md opens verbatim: "Pi packages bundle extensions, skills, prompt templates, and themes so you can share them through npm or git." The deliverable-2 survey (which community assets are worth adopting) is the weakest-covered part of the research question — the mechanism is proven, the marketplace census is not.

findings.claim: DESIGN PHILOSOPHY relevant to adoption: pi "ships with powerful defaults but skips features like sub agents and plan mode" by design — the intended adaptation path is extensions/skills/prompt-templates/themes and third-party pi packages rather than forking. This matches the seat's needs (deterministic gates at boundaries, custom confirmation flows) but means Claude Code niceties (built-in permission prompts, sub-agents, plan mode, ambient MCP) are all bring-your-own.
findings.evidence: Verbatim: "Pi ships with powerful defaults but skips features like sub agents and plan mode" plus explicit "No sub-agents" / "No plan mode" / "No permission popups" philosophy bullets, and "Pi is aggressively extensible so it doesn't have to dictate your workflow."

findings.claim: RECOMMENDATIONS (synthesis from the above): (1) ADOPT NOW via @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent from earendil-works/pi — never the deprecated @mariozechner scope; compaction, sessions, and providers (incl. openai-codex subscription and local models) meet the MUST-HAVEs out of the box. (2) BUDGET CUSTOM EXTENSION WORK for hooks parity: start from the shipped permission-gate.ts example for pre-tool-call gating; verify docs/extensions.md's full event list for post-edit and lifecycle/notification hooks before committing, and expect to write these yourself. (3) LEVERAGE: first-class llama.cpp for local; models.json custom-provider entries for ollama/LM Studio/vLLM (or the third-party pi-ollama-provider after review); the pi-packages mechanism for distributing your own extensions internally. (4) NO DEALBREAKERS found for the CLI on macOS + win32; the two watch items are the ungated-by-default posture (a real difference from Claude Code — gating exists only if you load a gate extension; align with the repo's un-bypassable-gate invariant before unattended use) and the absence of a verified standalone Agent UI (pi-web-ui is a lagging component library — plan to build any UI surface, or run TUI-only).
findings.vote: synthesis (derived from the 3-0 findings above, not independently voted)
findings.evidence: The recommendation's factual legs are each high-confidence; the confidence downgrade reflects that adoption fit (especially the four-hook parity effort estimate and UI plan) depends on the two unverified areas flagged in caveats.

result.caveats: Time-sensitivity: all metrics (stars, versions, push dates) are a 2026-09-01 snapshot of a project releasing at very high cadence; re-check before acting on version-specific details. Premise staleness: the research question's repo/npm coordinates (badlogic/pi-mono, @mariozechner) are superseded — every finding here was re-anchored to earendil-works/pi and @earendil-works. Hooks coverage is the biggest verification gap: only pre-tool-call blocking (tool_call) and session_before_compact were mechanically verified among the four required hook classes; post-edit format/lint/test triggers, session start/stop lifecycle events, and outward notification/observability hooks are plausible from the extensions event system but were NOT confirmed by any surviving claim — do not treat them as established. The community-ecosystem deliverable is thin: the packaging substrate and Discord are verified, but no census of third-party extensions/themes/forks survived verification, so 'which community assets to adopt' is answered only anecdotally. The 'Pi Agent UI' deliverable is partially unanswered: pi-web-ui exists but is a component library lagging ~3 months behind core; no standalone first-party UI app was verified on any platform. Some supporting evidence (docs/extensions.md blocking contract, docs/providers.md Ollama example, issue numbers) came from verifiers' corroboration fetches rather than the original voted claims — same primary-source class, but single-pass reads. One claim was refuted 0-3 (a wrong @earendil/pi package name), illustrating scope-name confusion risk in secondary coverage. Governance change risk: Earendil Works stewardship (post 'I've sold out') was verified as fact, but its licensing/roadmap implications were not examined.
openQuestions: What is the complete extension event list in docs/extensions.md — specifically, do events exist for post-edit triggers (e.g., after write/edit tool completion suitable for format/lint/test), session start/stop lifecycle, and outward notifications — and how much custom work does full Claude Code four-hook parity actually require?

What does the community extension ecosystem concretely contain as of Sept 2026 — is there a registry/awesome-list of pi packages, and are artifacts like pi-ollama-provider or an MCP-bridge extension (issue #563 lineage) mature enough to adopt versus writing in-house?
Is there (or is there a roadmap for) a first-party standalone Pi Agent UI application — web or desktop — beyond the pi-web-ui component library, and does whatever exists run on native Windows?

What changed under Earendil Works stewardship in licensing, governance, and commercial direction (the 2026-04-08 'I've sold out' transition), and does it pose any long-term platform-dependency risk for adopting pi as the primary agent?

refuted.claim: The npm package for the pi coding agent was renamed from @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent to @earendil/pi, so the @mariozechner npm scope named in the research question is no longer the current distribution channel for the agent.
